newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S.-Japan insurance talks to resume Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Japan insurance talks to resume Nov 25.

text.p: Japan and the United States will hold talks on their insurance dispute on November 25 and 26 in Tokyo, U.S. trade negotiator Ira Shapiro said on Thursday.

But Shapiro said he could not say whether he was hopeful or not about a successful outcome. "I would not characterise myself as hopeful or not," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum meeting in Manila.
He said he would not rule out the possibility that the issue might have to be resolved at a higher level.

"I think it's certainly a possibility that ministers will be involved at some point," Shapiro said after meeting Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato in Manila. The insurance talks will be between Shapiro and Eisuke Sakakibara of Japan's Finance Ministry. The last talks were in San Francisco on November 14 and 16.

Referring to the Japanese government's deregulation drive, Shapiro said "We will be talking about what it means for the insurance sector." Washington is pressing Tokyo to liberalise its primary insurance markets before the niche "third" sector, where U.S. firms have a strong presence, is opened up.
